title: 6 Best Deck Paints in 2026: Matched to Your Deck's Condition
metaDescription: Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid tops 6 deck paints for most sound wood decks. Picks include solid stains, porch enamels and resurfacers for old, cracked decks.
keywords: deck paint that fills in cracks
best deck paint for old decks
what paint sticks to unsanded wood patio deck
intro:
The best deck paint for most sound wood decks is Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid, a waterborne solid stain that gives one even color while staying thin and flexible enough to move with the boards. BEHR Premium Solid Color is the value alternative, and BEHR DeckOver is the resurfacer for old decks with cracks.

Painting a deck is hard to undo. On sound, dry wood with the right coating it buys years of color; on a damp or rotting deck it peels by next summer. Below are six picks matched to deck condition, plus a quick triage, why deck paint peels, prep, traction, coverage and when to skip paint entirely.
quickAnswer: For a sound deck that needs one color, use Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid or the cheaper BEHR Premium Solid Color. For covered porches, use a floor enamel such as BEHR Porch and Patio or Valspar Porch, Floor and Patio. Use a resurfacer like BEHR DeckOver or KILZ Over Armor only on rough decks with sound framing and dry wood.

| BEHR Premium Solid Color | Solid color on a budget | Acrylic solid stain, Home Depot tinting |
| BEHR Premium Advanced DeckOver | Old, checked, splintered decks | Thick resurfacer, fills cracks up to about 1/4 inch per Behr |

Three different products get sold as deck paint: solid stain, porch and floor enamel, and thick resurfacer. Solid stain is the default for open, sunny decks; floor enamel belongs under a roof; resurfacers are for decks that are structurally fine but cosmetically worn out.

If your boards still have good grain, a semi-transparent product from our [best deck stain rankings](/best-deck-stain-reviews/) never peels and keeps your options open.

sections.heading: The 6 Best Deck Paints in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
Picks are ranked on manufacturer data sheets, label coverage and recoat guidance, published warranty terms and patterns in owner feedback over several seasons. No exposure panels were run for this guide. Each product is matched to the deck condition it suits, because the right coating for a sound deck is the wrong one for a cracked one.

### Best Overall: Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid Deck and Siding Stain

Arborcoat Solid is Benjamin Moore's top waterborne solid stain for exterior wood, and it ranks first because it suits the most common deck painting job: a structurally sound deck with weathered or mismatched boards that needs one even color.

A solid stain like this hides the grain but stays thinner and more flexible than a true paint, so it moves with the boards and lets the wood texture show through. Benjamin Moore dealers tint it across a wide palette, and the same product is made for siding and railings, which makes matching the whole deck simple. Owners and painting contractors commonly describe it as easy to brush or roll evenly, and as aging by wearing gradually in traffic lanes rather than peeling in sheets. It cleans up with soap and water. It is a premium product sold only through dealers, and like every film it depends on clean, dry, well-prepared wood. It will not save a deck that stays wet.

**Pros:** thin, flexible film that follows the board texture; tints to a wide range of colors; made for decks and siding; soap-and-water cleanup; strong reputation with painting contractors.

**Cons:** sold through Benjamin Moore dealers only; premium price; still needs careful prep and dry wood.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Benjamin+Moore+Arborcoat+solid+deck+stain&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Value: BEHR Premium Solid Color Waterproofing Stain and Sealer

BEHR Premium Solid Color is the solid deck coating most homeowners can buy today. It is an acrylic sold and tinted at Home Depot, so the color range is wide and touch-up cans are easy to find.

It hides grain and mismatched boards while staying thinner than a floor paint, and it cleans up with soap and water. On railings, fences and siding, owners tend to be pleased with how long it holds color. On sunny horizontal decking the feedback is more mixed, with the main traffic paths often needing a recoat after a few seasons. Most peeling complaints come from decks where it went over an old penetrating stain or onto damp wood, which is a prep problem rather than a formula one. Strip or fully weather the old finish, sand lightly, let the wood dry and apply two thin coats. For a solid-color deck on a reasonable budget, it is the practical pick.

**Pros:** sold at every Home Depot; wide color range with in-store tinting; acrylic with soap-and-water cleanup; works on decks, fences and siding; moderate price.

**Cons:** shorter life on sunny floors than on vertical surfaces per owners; needs two coats; can peel over old penetrating stain.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=BEHR+Premium+solid+color+deck+stain&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Resurfacer for Old Decks: BEHR Premium Advanced DeckOver

DeckOver is the best-known deck resurfacer, a thick acrylic coating meant to give a worn-out but structurally sound deck a second life. Behr says it fills cracks up to about a quarter inch, and its textured surface hides checking, rough grain and splinters that ordinary paint would outline. That is why it shows up for searches about deck paint that fills in cracks.

The texture also improves grip on stairs and around pools, and it works on concrete as well as wood. Its history is a fair warning: resurfacers as a category, including earlier formulas from major brands, drew class-action complaints over peeling, and owner reviews still split between decks that look good for years and decks that lift within a season. The difference usually comes down to moisture and prep. It needs clean, dry wood free of old stain, every board edge coated and the label spread rate followed closely. Coverage is low, often 75 square feet per gallon or less per coat, so total product cost runs high.

**Pros:** thick body fills checks and small cracks; textured finish improves traction; locks down splinters; works on wood and concrete; wide color range.

**Cons:** low coverage raises total cost; very hard to remove; earlier resurfacer formulas drew class-action complaints over peeling.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=BEHR+Premium+Advanced+DeckOver&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Covered Porches: BEHR Porch and Patio Floor Paint, Low-Lustre Enamel

BEHR Porch and Patio Floor Paint is a one-part acrylic latex enamel made to stand up to foot traffic, and it is the right product for a covered porch, screened room or deck under a roof.

The low-lustre finish is smooth and easy to clean, and the same paint works on concrete steps and patios, so one color can tie an entry together. Because it is a true paint rather than a stain, it forms a slightly harder film. Under cover, that is an advantage: it resists scuffs and chair legs. On an open deck in full sun, the harder film is less tolerant of the boards swelling and shrinking, and cracking is more likely. On bare wood, use the exterior primer the label recommends, and a stain-blocking primer under light colors on cedar or redwood. Add an anti-slip additive for steps and anywhere that gets wet, since a smooth enamel is slick when damp.

**Pros:** smooth, scuff-resistant enamel; works on wood and concrete; tints to a wide range; easy cleanup and low odor; good for screened and covered porches.

**Cons:** slippery when wet without an additive; harder film can crack on open, sunny decks; primer usually needed on bare wood.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=BEHR+porch+and+patio+floor+paint&tag=sktiger-20)

### Budget Resurfacer: KILZ Over Armor Textured Wood and Concrete Coating

KILZ Over Armor sits between floor paint and a full resurfacer. It goes on thicker than paint and leaves a sand-textured, slip-resistant finish that hides rough grain, small checks and light splintering, without building as thick a layer as the heaviest resurfacers.

That makes it a sensible match for a deck with moderate wear that does not need deep crack filling. The texture is a plus on stairs and around pools, and it works on wood and concrete, which helps where a deck steps down onto a slab. Owner feedback follows the familiar resurfacer pattern: clean, dry, well-prepared decks tend to hold up, and decks coated over old stain or damp wood tend to peel. Follow the spread rate, coat board edges and ends, and stick to two coats. Expect it to be hard to strip if you ever change course, and expect coverage well below a standard paint.

**Pros:** textured, slip-resistant finish; hides minor cracks and rough grain; costs less than heavier resurfacers; works on wood and concrete; sold at major home centers.

**Cons:** thinner build than DeckOver, so it fills less; moisture-sensitive like any thick film; hard to remove.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=KILZ+Over+Armor+textured+coating&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best at Lowe's: Valspar Porch, Floor and Patio Latex Paint

Valspar Porch, Floor and Patio is the floor enamel Lowe's shoppers reach for, filling the same role as the BEHR porch paint across the street. It is an acrylic latex designed to resist scuffing on floors and steps, tinted in store to a broad range of colors.

Like any true floor paint, it does its best work on covered porches, partly shaded decks and steps rather than open decks in full sun, where a solid stain handles the wood's movement better. Owners generally describe it as easy to roll, with good hiding in two coats over a primed surface. The common complaints are slipperiness on wet steps and peeling where it went over an old finish without enough prep. Add an anti-slip additive to the last coat on stairs and pool surrounds, and use a stain-blocking primer on cedar or redwood. It is a good choice if you want porch paint for a deck and porch that share one color.

**Pros:** widely available at Lowe's with in-store tinting; durable acrylic latex floor formula; works on wood and concrete; moderate price; soap-and-water cleanup.

**Cons:** needs anti-slip additive in wet areas; best on covered or shaded surfaces; primer needed on bare or tannin-rich wood.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Valspar+porch+floor+and+patio+paint&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: Should You Paint Your Deck? A Five-Minute Triage
sections.body:
Paint is a good choice for a structurally sound deck with weathered, mismatched or previously coated boards. It is a poor choice for a deck with soft wood, constant dampness or an old finish that still repels water.

### Probe for rot

Push a screwdriver into boards near the house, around posts, on stair treads and wherever water pools. If it sinks more than about an eighth of an inch with light pressure, that wood is soft. Coating it hides rot for a season while it spreads. Replace soft boards and check the joists below.

### Read the old finish

If water beads on the boards, a sealer or stain is still active and paint will not bond. If an old coating is peeling in sheets, everything loose must come off. Bare gray boards are the easiest to paint after cleaning and a light sanding.

### Check moisture and airflow

Low decks over grass or wet soil, or with tight board gaps, stay damp from below, and paint traps that moisture until it blisters off. A pin moisture meter reading in the low to mid teens is a reasonable target before any film.

| Deck condition | Best coating type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sound, bare, graying wood | Solid stain or porch paint | Clean, light sand, two thin coats |
| Sound, old stain worn off | Solid stain | Strip remaining stain first |
| Checked, splintered, small cracks | Thick resurfacer | Only if structure is sound |
| Soft spots or chronic damp | None yet | Fix wood and drainage first |
| Covered porch floor | Porch and floor enamel | Less sun means longer life |

sections.heading: Solid Stain, Porch Paint or Resurfacer: Which Deck Coating Do You Need?
sections.body:
Use solid stain on open decks in sun, porch and floor enamel under a roof, and a resurfacer only on rough decks with sound framing. They are not interchangeable.

### Solid color deck stain

Usually acrylic or acrylic-modified, it hides the grain but stays thinner and more flexible than paint, so it follows the board texture. Most solid stains can be recoated without stripping as long as the surface is sound. For bare or freshly stripped decks in full sun, this is the default.

### Porch and floor paint

A true paint, typically a one-part acrylic latex enamel formulated to resist scuffs. It forms a smoother, harder film than solid stain, which shines on covered porches and screened rooms. On open decks in harsh climates that harder film cracks more readily as the wood moves.

### Resurfacers

Thick-bodied coatings built up to many times the thickness of paint. They fill checks, lock down splinters and add a textured, grippy surface. They also have the most checkered history, and success depends heavily on dry wood and careful prep.

### Do not mix systems

A resurfacer over a peeling solid stain inherits that stain's weak bond. A porch paint over a resurfacer may look fine and then crack as the thick layer moves. Choose one system for the whole deck, stay in the same family when you recoat, and use the primer the maker names.

If you only want to change the color of a deck with good grain and will recoat every few years, a semi-transparent stain is the safer path; it fades instead of peeling.

sections.heading: Why Does Deck Paint Peel?
sections.body:
Nearly every peeling deck traces back to moisture getting behind the film. Paint fails from behind, not from on top.

### How it happens

Wood swells when it absorbs water and shrinks when it dries. A paint film flexes far less than the wood under it. When water gets in through a crack, an uncoated end, a nail hole or the underside of a board, it pushes the film off from behind, and summer sun softens the coating and finishes the job.

### Coat every face you can reach

On new or replacement boards, prime or seal all four sides and both ends before installing, or at least the ends. On existing decks, coat board edges and ends, not just the top. Water through bare ends is one of the most common causes of peeling that starts at board tips and spreads inward.

### Do not paint over a surface that will not hold it

Old penetrating stain, waxy water repellents, mill glaze on new lumber and chalky residue from failed coatings all block adhesion. That answers a common question about what paint sticks to an unsanded patio deck: on smooth or previously sealed boards, nothing sticks reliably until you clean, scuff-sand and confirm water soaks in. The tape test confirms it: press masking tape onto a prepped and coated test patch, let it dry and pull it off fast. If paint comes off on the tape, the surface needs more prep.

### Keep coats thin

Two thin coats beat one heavy coat for everything except resurfacers, which are meant to go on thick but still within the label's spread rate. Overbuilt paint cracks as it ages, and cracks let water in.

sections.heading: How Do You Prep and Prime a Deck for Paint?
sections.body:
Clean, remove anything loose, sand, repair, let the wood dry and prime when the label says so. Prep is most of the job.

### Clean

A deck cleaner and scrub brush remove dirt, mildew and chalky old finish. Rinse at low pressure with a wide fan tip, held well back and moving with the grain. A [surface cleaner attachment](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/) keeps the rinse even across a big floor at reduced pressure.

### Remove and sand

A deck stripper handles old solid stain and loose paint over a whole surface; a scraper and sander handle smaller areas. Sand with about 60 to 80 grit to open the wood and knock down raised fibers, then sweep and vacuum the gaps. A stripped deck also needs a brightener to neutralize the stripper.

### Repair

Reset or replace popped nails with deck screws, swap cracked or soft boards, and fill small holes in railings with an exterior filler from our [wood filler picks](/best-wood-filler/). On walking surfaces, filler tends to pop out, so replacing a split board is the better fix.

### Let it dry

Most coating labels want at least 48 hours of dry weather after washing or stripping. New pressure-treated lumber may need weeks or months before it accepts any film.

### Prime

Many solid stains and resurfacers are self-priming on bare wood, while porch paints often call for an exterior primer. Cedar and redwood bleed tannins that discolor light colors, so use a stain-blocking primer under pale shades on those species.

sections.heading: How Do You Apply Deck Paint So It Lasts?
sections.body:
Paint on a mild, dry day, cut in edges and gaps first, roll a few boards at a time along their full length, and apply two coats.

### Weather window

Most acrylic deck coatings want air and surface temperatures of at least 50 degrees, sometimes higher, and need to stay above that overnight. Avoid direct midday sun, which dries the surface before the film levels, and evenings when dew will form before it sets.

### Technique

1. Brush the board edges and ends first.
2. Roll two or three boards at a time along their full length so you always roll into wet paint.
3. Clear paint that bridges board gaps with a brush or thin putty knife; a bridged gap traps water and cracks.
4. Do railings and vertical parts first, then the floor, and finish at the exit.
5. Wait the full recoat time and apply a second coat.

### Resurfacer specifics

Use the roller nap and spread rate the maker specifies. Spreading too thin to stretch a gallon leaves a weak layer; too thick to fill a crack in one pass invites failure. Fill larger cracks first with the maker's filler or a spot coat.

### Cure time

Many coatings feel dry in a few hours but take several days to harden. Light foot traffic is usually fine after a day. Keep furniture, grills and planters off longer, and rugs off for at least a week.

### Coverage

Standard porch paints and solid stains often list roughly 250 to 400 square feet per gallon per coat on smooth surfaces; resurfacers may list as little as 50 to 75. Railings with pickets can add nearly half again to the floor area, so measure everything and buy from one batch.

sections.heading: How Do You Make a Painted Deck Less Slippery and Cooler?
sections.body:
Choose a textured coating or add an anti-slip additive to the final coat, and pick a mid-tone color rather than a very dark one for a sunny deck.

### Traction

A smooth painted deck is more slippery when wet than bare wood. For stairs, pool surrounds and shaded decks that hold dew, use a textured coating such as DeckOver or Over Armor, or mix a fine anti-slip aggregate into the last coat of paint or solid stain. Most paint makers sell a compatible additive. Stir often, because it settles in the tray. Keeping the deck clean helps too, since algae, mildew and wet leaves make any coating slick.

### Heat and color

Dark solid colors on a south or west-facing deck can get uncomfortably hot under bare feet, and darker films also expand and contract more through daily temperature swings, which stresses the coating. Mid-tone grays, tans and browns stay cooler and hide dirt and pollen better than very light colors.

### Light colors

Pale decks show every leaf stain and footprint, and on cedar or redwood they can yellow as tannins bleed through. If you want a light deck, use a stain-blocking primer and plan on more frequent cleaning. Many owners pair a darker floor with lighter railings, which also hides wear where people walk.

### Test first

Paint a scrap board or an out-of-the-way stair tread and look at it in morning and afternoon light. Solid stains and floor paints often dry a shade different from the chip.

sections.heading: How Long Does Deck Paint Last, and When Is Paint the Wrong Answer?
sections.body:
On an open, sunny deck, solid stain and porch paint typically last about three to five years before the traffic lanes need recoating, and longer on covered porches. Resurfacers can last several years on dry, well-prepared wood but fail fast when moisture gets behind them.

### Upkeep

Wash a painted deck once or twice a year with a mild deck cleaner and soft brush, and clear debris from board gaps so water drains. Touch up chips at stair noses and traffic lanes early: sand the edges, spot prime bare wood and apply thin coats of the same product. Write down the product, color, batch and date for future matches.

### Know the exit plan

Removing a solid coating means chemical stripping and heavy sanding, and resurfacers are especially stubborn. If you might want natural wood back someday, a penetrating finish from our [deck sealer guide](/best-deck-sealant/) is the better choice now.

### When to skip paint

- **Constantly shaded, poorly ventilated decks** stay damp, grow mildew and peel early.
- **New cedar, redwood or tropical hardwood** was chosen for its grain; a toned penetrating finish keeps it looking like what it is.
- **Decks you will not maintain** fail in patches that are harder to restore than a faded stain.
- **Bouncy or loose decks** crack thick resurfacers; fix the framing first.
- **Composite decking** should not be painted unless the board maker publishes a coating system.

If more than about a quarter of the boards are cracked, cupped or soft, new decking over sound framing may cost less over the next decade than repeated resurfacing.

mistakes.title: Painting over a finish that still repels water
mistakes.body: If water beads on the boards, an old sealer or penetrating stain is still active and paint will not bond to it. The coating may look fine for weeks and then peel in sheets. Strip it or let it weather fully, clean, sand lightly and tape-test a small patch first.

mistakes.title: Coating a deck that stays damp
mistakes.body: Low decks over wet ground, decks under trees and boards with tight gaps hold moisture from below. A film traps it and blisters off from the underside. Fix drainage and airflow, check with a moisture meter, and use a penetrating finish instead of paint on chronically damp decks.

mistakes.title: Spreading a resurfacer too thin
mistakes.body: Resurfacers rely on a set thickness to fill cracks and resist wear. Stretching a gallon over more area leaves a thin layer that wears through and fails to bridge checks. Use the roller and spread rate on the label, fill larger cracks first and buy enough for two full coats.

mistakes.title: Leaving board ends and edges bare
mistakes.body: Water that enters through uncoated ends and edges gets behind the film and pushes it off, starting at the board tips. Brush coating into the ends, sides and gaps of every board, not just the top face, and coat the ends of replacement boards before installing them.

mistakes.title: Choosing a very dark color for a sunny deck
mistakes.body: Very dark solid colors on south or west-facing decks get uncomfortably hot underfoot and expand and contract more each day, which stresses the film. Mid-tone colors stay cooler, hide dirt and pollen better and tend to last longer. Test a sample board in full sun first.

faqs.q: What is the best deck paint?
faqs.a: Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid is the best deck paint for most sound wood decks because it gives an even color while staying thin and flexible. BEHR Premium Solid Color is the value alternative. For covered porches, use a floor enamel such as BEHR Porch and Patio, and for rough decks with cracks, a resurfacer like BEHR DeckOver.

faqs.q: What is the best deck paint for old decks?
faqs.a: For an old deck that is structurally sound but rough, checked or splintered, a resurfacer such as BEHR Premium Advanced DeckOver or KILZ Over Armor is the best choice, because it fills small cracks and adds traction. If the boards are only weathered and gray, a solid stain such as Arborcoat Solid is simpler and easier to maintain.

faqs.q: Is there a deck paint that fills in cracks?
faqs.a: Yes. Deck resurfacers are thick coatings made to fill checks and small cracks, and Behr says DeckOver fills cracks up to about a quarter inch. They only work on dry, well-prepared wood with sound framing, and they are very hard to remove later. Replace boards with large splits rather than trying to fill them.

faqs.q: Is it better to paint or stain a deck?
faqs.a: Stain is usually better on decks in good condition because it soaks in or forms a thin, flexible layer that fades rather than peels. Paint or solid stain makes sense when boards are weathered, mismatched or already coated with film. Paint gives a uniform color but commits you to film maintenance and heavy stripping if you change course.

faqs.q: How long does deck paint last?
faqs.a: On an open, sunny deck, solid stain and porch paint typically last about three to five years before the main traffic areas need recoating, and longer on covered porches. Resurfacers can last several years on dry, well-prepared wood but fail quickly when moisture gets behind them. Prep, sun and foot traffic matter more than the brand.

faqs.q: What is the best paint for decks and porches?
faqs.a: For a covered porch or a deck under a roof, a porch and floor enamel such as BEHR Porch and Patio Floor Paint or Valspar Porch, Floor and Patio is the best choice, because its smooth film resists scuffs. For open decks in full sun, a solid stain such as Arborcoat Solid handles the wood's movement better.

faqs.q: What paint sticks to an unsanded wood deck?
faqs.a: No paint bonds reliably to an unsanded deck that still has mill glaze, old sealer or a chalky failed finish. Clean the deck, sand lightly with 60 to 80 grit, let it dry and make sure water soaks in before coating. Self-priming solid stains such as Arborcoat Solid or BEHR Solid then bond well to the prepared wood.

bottomLine: For a sound deck that needs one even color, Benjamin Moore Arborcoat Solid is the best coating here, with BEHR Premium Solid Color as the value pick you can buy today. Covered porches are better served by a true floor enamel such as BEHR Porch and Patio or Valspar Porch, Floor and Patio, and resurfacers like DeckOver and Over Armor earn their place only on rough decks with good framing and dry wood. The coating is the last step, not the first: probe for rot, fix drainage, strip what is failing, coat every edge and let the wood dry. If the grain is still worth seeing, use stain instead, because going from stain to paint later is far easier than the reverse. Matching the fence? See our [fence stain picks](/best-fence-stain/).
